rows.Finding description: At 18 DIV, eight-hour DQ-BSA degradation signal in dendrites showed no significant difference between ApoE4 and ApoE3 neurons; n counts embryos.
rows.Finding quote: When we compared our ApoE groups at 18 DIV there were no differences in the total intensities of DQ BSA in dendrites or cell bodies between ApoE KO, ApoE3, and ApoE4 neurons after 8 h (Fig. 2, G and H).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in dendritic DQ-BSA degradation)
rows.Experimental system: Primary embryonic mouse hippocampal/cortical mixed cultures with human APOE targeted replacement; primary dendrites at 18 DIV; 25 μg/ml DQ-BSA for eight hours.

rows.Finding description: After three-day cholesterol supplementation, average somatic LAMP1-positive compartment size showed no significant difference between ApoE4 and ApoE3 neurons; n counts embryos.
rows.Finding quote: Even though cholesterol seemed to have an impact on endosomes, including a lower number of early endosomes (Fig. 6K), larger LAMP1+ vesicles (Fig. 6L) without altering the number (Fig. S4E), and reduced degradation of DQ-BSA after 8 h (Fig. 6M), we detected similar changes between ApoE KO, ApoE3, and ApoE4.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4 under cholesterol loading) -> (no change in somatic LAMP1-positive compartment size)
rows.Experimental system: Primary embryonic mouse hippocampal/cortical mixed cultures with human APOE targeted replacement; cholesterol–BSA 12.5 μg/ml for three days ending around 25 DIV; LAMP1 size normalized to untreated ApoE3.

rows.Finding description: APOE44 microglia had lower HEXB protein abundance than APOE33 microglia in proteomics using three wells per genotype; enzyme activity was not measured.
rows.Finding quote: These data were in agreement with our scRNAseq results, also indicating that lysosomal and endosomal pathways were being downregulated (i.e., LAMP1, LAMP2, HEXA, HEXB) (Figures 3I-K, S3C, Table S6).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (lower lysosomal HEXB protein abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Human male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia; baseline whole-cell proteomic HEXB abundance; three wells per genotype. Donor age, AD status and culture duration were not stated.

rows.Finding description: Proteomic comparison of three wells per genotype identified lower lysosomal/endosomal protein abundance in APOE44 than APOE33 microglia, including LAMP1, LAMP2, HEXA and HEXB.
rows.Finding quote: These data were in agreement with our scRNAseq results, also indicating that lysosomal and endosomal pathways were being downregulated (i.e., LAMP1, LAMP2, HEXA, HEXB) (Figures 3I-K, S3C, Table S6).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (lower lysosomal/endosomal protein abundance, a surrogate of organelle function)
rows.Experimental system: Human male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia; baseline whole-cell proteomics; three wells per genotype. Protein abundance was measured rather than lysosomal enzyme activity. Donor age, AD status and culture duration were not stated.
rows.Data location: Supplementary Fig S3C, LAMP1, LAMP2, HEXA and HEXB

rows.Finding description: APOE44 microglia had higher LC3B protein abundance than APOE33 microglia in three wells per genotype, consistent with autophagosome accumulation but without direct autophagic flux measurement.
rows.Finding quote: Further, p62 (SQSTM1) and LC3B (MAP1LC3B2) were both upregulated, supporting a buildup of autophagosomes (Figure S3E).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (higher LC3B abundance, a surrogate consistent with autophagosome accumulation)
rows.Experimental system: Human male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia; baseline whole-cell proteomic LC3B abundance, identified in the paper as MAP1LC3B2, without reported LC3 turnover or flux measurement; three wells per genotype. Donor age and AD status were not stated.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: In six independent mouse-astrocyte experiments, human E4 showed higher intracellular N+C intermolecular FRET than E3, supporting increased apoE–apoE proximity without establishing aggregate burden or endo-lysosomal localization.
rows.Finding quote: When comparing the interactions between corresponding combinations of the apoE termini, intermolecular FRET was higher for E4 and lower for E2, with E3 adopting intermediate FRET levels.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher intracellular N+C intermolecular FRET in mouse astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Primary immortalized mouse astrocytes genetically null for endogenous apoE, transiently co-transfected with human RFP-apoE and apoE-GFP of the same isoform, E3 or E4, at a 1:1 ratio, 0.48 μg/cm2 each; collected 36 h after transfection, fixed in 2% PFA for 10 min, and analyzed by flow-cytometry FRET. Mouse strain and donor age not specified in supplied text; no endo-lysosomal localization.

Whole-cell measurement; no endosomal or lysosomal localization, acidic-pH manipulation, or donor-age characterization.

Conditioned medium collected 3–4 days after transfection, concentrated using 10-kDa filters, and captured overnight at 4 °C on protein G Dynabeads using anti-GFP antibody before flow-cytometry FRET. rows.Finding description: Cell-associated apoE measurements with and without lysosomal inhibitors contributed to the finding that apoE4 underwent less efficient lysosomal trafficking and degradation than apoE3 in mouse N2a cells.
rows.Finding quote: We found that apoE3 was transported into lysosomes and degraded more efficiently than apoE4 ( Fig. 7 , A and B ).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (less efficient lysosomal trafficking and degradation of apoE)
rows.Experimental system: Mouse N2a neuroblastoma cells prepared as in Fig 5A; recombinant human apoE3 or apoE4, 500 nM, with Aβ42, 500 nM, for 24 h, with or without lysosomal inhibitors; cell-associated human apoE measured by ELISA. Lipid metabolism was not measured.
rows.Data location: Fig 7A; Results interpretation jointly references Fig 7A and Fig 7B

rows.Finding description: Quantification of apoE colocalization with lysosomes showed less efficient lysosomal trafficking of apoE4 than apoE3 in mouse N2a cells during lysosomal inhibition.
rows.Finding quote: The more efficient trafficking of apoE3 than apoE4 was confirmed by immunostaining and confocal microscopy ( Fig. 7 , C and D ).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (lower lysosome-associated apoE)
rows.Experimental system: Mouse N2a neuroblastoma cells; recombinant human apoE3 or apoE4, 500 nM, with Aβ42, 500 nM, for 24 h with lysosomal inhibitors; apoE and LAMP1 immunostaining, confocal microscopy, and ImageJ quantification of lysosome-associated apoE. Lipid metabolism was not measured.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes impaired ARF6-related recycling of receptors between the cell surface and the endosome, compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Quantification showed greater Apoer2 surface-recycling impairment with ApoE4 than ApoE3 in inhibitor-free neurons across three independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: As shown in Figure 4D and E, physiological concentrations of ApoE3 (5 µg/ml) also impaired Apoer2 recycling to a small, but significant extent. This was also prevented by EMD87580 at the same concentration (3 µM) at which the effect of ApoE4 on Apoer2 recycling was completely neutralized (Figure 4D,E), suggesting that ApoE3 also, although to a minor extent, may lose solubility upon entering the early endosome, and that this is also prevented by pH lowering.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater reduction of surface-to-total Apoer2 ratio)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons, DIV9–14; cell-derived ApoE3 or ApoE4 and Reelin; quantified surface-to-total Apoer2 immunoblots in matched conditions without EMD87580.

rows.Finding description: Figure 2C quantifies surface-to-total Lrp1 levels across three independent experiments. The authors describe levels with ApoE3 and ApoE4 as comparable.
rows.Finding quote: Other ApoE receptors, such as low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (Lrp1) and low-density lipoprotein receptor (Ldlr), as well as the endocytic receptor for transferrin (TfR) and insulin receptor (IR) exhibit comparable surface levels in the presence of ApoE3 or ApoE4.
rows.Finding summary: Surface-to-total Lrp1 levels were comparable with ApoE3 and ApoE4 under the Reelin protocol.
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons, DIV9–14; cell-derived ApoE3 or ApoE4 plus Reelin; quantified surface-biotinylation immunoblots; Lrp1 is not driven into endocytosis by Reelin.

rows.Finding description: Quantification of three independent co-immunoprecipitation experiments showed greater persistence of ApoE4 than ApoE3 association with neuronal Apoer2.
rows.Finding quote: The delayed recycling of Apoer2 was also apparent by the prolonged retention of cell-derived ApoE4 compared to cell-derived ApoE3 in Apoer2-containing intracellular compartments as shown by co-immunoprecipitation of neuronal lysates (Figure 2D,E).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater Apoer2-associated ApoE retention)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons, DIV9–14; ApoE3 or ApoE4 at 5 µg/ml for 3 hr; quantified anti-Apoer2 co-immunoprecipitation and ApoE immunoblotting.

rows.Finding description: EMD87580 restored surface GluA2/3 in ApoE4-treated primary rat neurons across three independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: EMD87580 and the NHE6-specific shRNAs completely restored Apoer2 and glutamate receptor surface expression, while the scrambled shRNA had no effect (Panel B and quantified in Panels C-F).
rows.Finding summary: (NHE inhibition in ApoE4-treated neurons) -> (restored surface GluA2/3)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons, DIV9–14; ordinarily 3 µM EMD87580 for 1 hr before cell-derived ApoE4 and Reelin; GluA2/3 surface biotinylation and quantified surface-to-total immunoblotting.
rows.Data location: Fig 6F, EMD87580 versus ApoE4 without inhibitor

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Quantification of the tandem LC3 reporter indicated impaired autophagic processing under ApoE4 plus PHF in the ApoE isoform experiment, using 10–12 fields from three biological replicates.
rows.Finding quote: We detected increased autophagosomes (remaining yellow dots in Fig. 5i) relative to autolysosomes in microglia treated with ApoE4 in the presence of PHF, indicating impaired autophagy lysosomal pathway.
rows.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4, with PHF) -> (impaired autophagy lysosomal pathway)
rows.Experimental system: Mouse BV2 immortalized microglial cells, not human cells. Recombinant human ApoE3 or ApoE4, 4 μg/ml for 6 h in 10% FBS, washing and 4 h in fresh medium, then 1 μg/ml tau PHF for 24 h. Tandem mRFP-GFP-LC3 reporter puncta were quantified from fixed-cell fluorescence images; the authors interpret the autophagosome/autolysosome distribution as autophagic flux.

rows.Finding description: Capsaicin decreased lysosomal cholesterol accumulation in ApoE4-plus-PHF BV2 microglia, imaged in 8–18 fields from three biological replicates; this is a pharmacological rescue with ApoE4 exposure fixed.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE4 significantly increased the accumulation of cholesterol in lysosomes of microglia treated with PHF compared to ApoE3, while treatment with capsaicin significantly decreased it (Fig. 5k, l).
rows.Finding summary: (vehicle -> capsaicin, with ApoE4 and PHF) -> (decreased lysosomal cholesterol accumulation)
rows.Experimental system: Mouse BV2 immortalized microglial cells loaded with recombinant human ApoE4, 4 μg/ml for 6 h with 10% FBS, washed and incubated for 4 h. Vehicle or 1 μM capsaicin was applied for 30 min before 1 μg/ml tau PHF for 24 h. Confocal filipin III and LysoTracker imaging assessed cholesterol accumulation in lysosomes.

rows.Finding description: Dextran-Alexa 555 imaging showed no significant difference in the labeled lysosomal compartment between APOE4 and APOE3 iAstrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: Immunofluorescent detection of lysosomes by LAMP2 (Figure 4C) or Dextran-Alexa 555 (Figure S3) showed no difference between genotypes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in the dextran-labeled lysosomal compartment in iAstrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human isogenic, monoallelic APOE3 (BIONi010-C-2) and APOE4 (BIONi010-C-4) iPSC-derived astrocytes after 44-day differentiation, at baseline; Dextran-Alexa 555 lysosomal labeling. The stated labeling protocol uses 0.2 mg/mL dextran overnight followed by a 14-hour chase. The supplementary image, legend, and panel-specific quantification details are absent from the supplied text.

rows.Finding description: Removing extracellular lipids produced no significant difference in GPN-estimated acidic-store calcium content in APOE3 astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: Surprisingly, measurement of Ca2+ stored inside acidic organelles using the GPN-elicited depletion showed no increased Ca2+ loading in APOE3 cells kept in KH (Fig. 7b) compared to APOE3 astrocytes kept in the presence of FBS, whereas, as expected, no difference was observed between the two conditions in APOE4 astrocytes (Fig. 7c).
rows.Finding summary: (FBS-containing medium -> lipid-free KH in APOE3 astrocytes) -> (no change in acidic-store calcium content)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3, studied alongside APOE4 cells; donor age unspecified; acute lipid-free Krebs medium versus DMEM with FBS, 200 μM GPN, fura-2/AM cytosolic calcium AUC.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: RAB7 immunocytochemistry quantification showed decreased late endosome marker levels in APOE4 versus APOE3 astrocytes across 18 wells per genotype.
rows.Finding quote: Compared to APOE3 astrocytes, APOE4 astrocytes showed decreased levels of all three downstream endosomal compartment markers (RAB11, RAB7, LAMP1) indicating dysfunction throughout the endocytic pathway.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (decreased RAB7-positive late endosome staining in human astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from KOLF2.1J and AG09173 isogenic homozygous APOE3/APOE4 line pairs; four-day serum withdrawal; fixed-cell RAB7 immunocytochemistry with confocal image intensity analysis normalized to cell area.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Representative LAMP1–TMED5 PLA images illustrate the higher APOE4 signal quantified across three independent differentiations in Fig. 6B.
rows.Finding quote: In concordance with our observations in Neuro-2a cells, we found that APOE4 iPSC-derived neurons harbored less lysosomal LGALS3BP and more lysosomal TMED5 compared to their APOE3 counterparts (Figure 6B,C).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosomal TMED5 PLA signal)
rows.Experimental system: Human female APOE4 and isogenic APOE3 iPSC-derived mixed neuronal cultures at DIV49; representative LAMP1-TMED5 PLA confocal images.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Combined CCCP and chloroquine treatment produced less LC3-II accumulation in APOE4 than APOE3 astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: Accordingly, APOE3 astrocytes treated with CCCP combined with chloroquine showed increased accumulation of LC3-II compared to APOE4 astrocytes, indicating higher autophagic flux30 (Fig. 3d).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LC3-II accumulation during combined CCCP and chloroquine treatment)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse APOE3/APOE4 astrocyte lines; 10 μM chloroquine for 48 h with 7.5 μM CCCP during the final 24 h; LC3 immunoblotting; n = 3, experimental unit unspecified.
